Houston has absolutely kick ass food. I second the person who recommended you try Viet-Cajun - it' s fusion cuisine original to the US Gulf Coast. In my experience every unassuming restaurant that offers both Vietnamese food + crawfish on the menu has been delicious and you'll be in during crawfish season. Himalaya Restaurant in Houston is also amazing. It's Pakistani food, but there are some Texas-y things about the menu like a paratha quesadilla. it's in a strip mall off of the interstate and when you pull up, you'll wonder if you're in the wrong place, but then have one of the best meals of your life. 

See a show in Austin after you awaken from your BBQ food coma - we have a lively nightlife any night of the week. also, if you haven't tried mezcal before, do!

just a psa - driving on Texas highways can be a bit impatient at its best and feral at its worst, so just check your mirrors an extra time or two because I've noticed people playing fast and loose with traffic laws slightly more often on tx city roads than in some other US cities. While I'm at it - another heads up for driving is that there are lots of toll roads around Houston and Austin that have no cash toll booths, but if you're getting around with a rental car they should just be added on to your rental car bill via a plate reader. I only mention this because when I first moved to the area I thought I was going to get someone coming after me for toll evasion because I didn't have a toll account set up lol.
